messages.subject: Comparison Plot Visualizations
messages.body_plain:
Hi MSstats maintainers,

Is there a way to generate volcano plots that include protein names without overlap? I've messed around with "ProteinNameLoc" but this doesn't help. I'm using MSstats Daily 2.1.6 in R. I'd like to generate figure quality volcano plots without having to manually re-label points.

Thanks,

Scott

messages.subject: Re: Comparison Plot Visualizations
messages.body_plain:
Dear Scott,

Unfortunately, MSstats doesn't have the option for adjusting the location of Protein Name individually. 'ProteinNameLoc' is the distance between the points and Protein Name for all points. Now what I suggest is to re-label Protein Name manually or to modify the R codes of groupComparisonPlots from source file for your dataset If you are used to write R codes. We will try to add this options or improve for later version.

Thank you for your feedback.

Meena

messages.body_plain:
Dear Sophie,

If a peptide is present in a modified and a non-modified form, you can include both forms into protein quantification if these forms have different identifies (i.e. the string of characters that defines the peptide ion is changed to reflect the modification). However you should be careful with this approach, because modifications can distort the quantitative profiles of a protein between runs, and introduce more interferences than benefit.

messages.subject: Re: MS1 Label Free Dataset
messages.body_plain:
Olga and Lorenzo,

I found this thread after running into the same problem with my label-free MS1 dataset and think I've found a work-around. I'm performing the MS1 analysis in Skyline, exporting the results, and running MSstats.daily 2.1.6 in R.

I was able to narrow down this error to two problems with the imported dataset:
If there are duplicate peptides in the document (i.e. between protein isoforms), MSstats flags the peptides as duplicates. To get rid of duplicates, I used the "remove repeated peptides" feature in Skyline (Edit-->Refine-->Remove repeated peptides). This option will remove all repeated peptides except for the first occurrence.
If a peptide has multiple charge states (i.e. +2 and +3), MSstats flags the peptide as a duplicate. Lorenzo, it looks this is your problem. There are +2 and +3 peptides in your document (I copied one example below). Instead of changing "PrecursorCharge" and "ProductCharge" columns to "NA" like the MSstats manual suggests, I kept the charges in the document.
Peptide with multiple charges:

CNAVGEVKDYEPPFGSK_2_precursor [M+1]_2, CNAVGEVKDYEPPFGSK_2_precursor [M+2]_2, CNAVGEVKDYEPPFGSK_2_precursor_2, CNAVGEVKDYEPPFGSK_3_precursor [M+1]_3, CNAVGEVKDYEPPFGSK_3_precursor [M+2]_3, CNAVGEVKDYEPPFGSK_3_precursor_3

Olga, assuming a peptide is unique, how will multiply-charged peptides affect protein level quantification?

Scott

messages.body_plain:
Dear Scott,

Thank you for your post, this is indeed the right solution. MSstats treats all peptide ions as different features. I.e., a peptide with charge +2 and a same peptide with charge +3 will be considered different features. We do not distinguish the nature of the features (different peptides sequences or different charges).

HTH
Sincerely
Olga

messages.subject: Re: Normalization to global standard proteins
messages.body_plain:
Hi Anuli,

“globalStandardProtein” normalization is for endogenous peptide only. "global standard proteins" option doesn't not normalize the reference peptides because first purpose of this option is to normalize for label-free experiment. For label-based experiment, reference intensities are just used when we get the relative quantification of protein in order to handle MS run variation. If you have label-based experiment and global standard proteins, I can suggest that you need two step normalizations. First, normalization for reference peptides (normalization="equalizeMedian") and then normalization with global standard protein. Unfortunately, now you can use only one of them. We will update MSstats for two step normalizations.

Thanks,

Meena

messages.subject: Citing MSstats - publications in Bioinformatics
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats users,

First, I'm happy to announce our recent publications in Bioinformatics about MSstats R-package and external tools in Skyline. Now they are available in online.
1. M. Choi et al. "MSstats: an R package for statistical analysis for quantitative mass spectrometry-based proteomic experiments. <http://bioinformatics.oxfordjournals.org/content/early/2014/05/02/bioinformatics.btu305.abstract>" Bioinformatics (2014), DOI: 10.1093/bioinformatics/btu305
2. D. Broudy and T.Killeen et al. "A framework for installable external tools in Skyline <http://bioinformatics.oxfordjournals.org/content/early/2014/05/09/bioinformatics.btu148.abstract>." Bioinformatics (2014), DOI: 10.1093/bioinformatics/btu148

Second, If you already had a plan to visit ASMS 2014 in Baltimore, please join us at Summer Skyline User Group Meeting <https://skyline.gs.washington.edu/labkey/project/home/software/Skyline/events/2014%20User%20Group%20Meeting%20at%20ASMS/begin.view?> (Sunday, June 15th, 2014 - registration required) as well. I will have 20 mins presentation about overview of MSstats and our group will be there also. I hope that we have a chance to meet you and hear your feedback and suggestion.

-- Meena
